goal: Make source-side per-file open, hydration, read, and size-drift failures nonfatal and accurately reported without corrupting neighboring payloads or destroying a valid destination copy.
recommended_approach: Keep the contract-v7 need ledger, explicit skip and failed-record terminators, exact-size shard buffering, same-handle source validation, staged whole-file commits, and the existing record_failure reporting path, but make staging dry-run-safe, budget it across parallel writers, use fixed-length securely-created temporary names, and define a descriptor-capable opened-source abstraction that preserves platform fast paths without reopening by path.
comparison: The reviewed plan has the right overall architecture and addresses the motivating corruption at its root, but it is not yet the best executable plan: its staging design omits existing dry-run guarantees and understates parallel disk usage, its proposed source-handle type cannot support the handle-based local cascade it requires, its temporary naming fails for valid long names, and canonical state omits two pending rulings.
material_changes: Specify a no-write RecordWriter and local short-circuit for dry-run mode, with regression guards proving no directories or staging files are created.
Replace the single-file staging-space assumption with an aggregate bound and admission policy covering all concurrent data-plane and local sink workers.
Define OpenedSourceFile as a descriptor-capable abstraction and refactor each platform copy path to consume that same opened handle without losing required fast paths.
Use a fixed-length, target-name-independent staging basename created with create-new semantics and collision retries.
Update every SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT entry in docs/STATE.md from pending rulings D1–D4 to D1–D6.

findings.title: The proposed record lifecycle can mutate the destination during dry runs
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:353 — FsTransferSink::begin_record is specified to open a staging file, while crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/sink.rs:1138 and :1377 deliberately return before parent creation or file creation in dry-run mode.
findings.predicted_failure: A remote or local --dry-run would create directories or temporary files, and cancellation could leave an orphan, violating the command's existing side-effect-free contract.
findings.better_approach: Have begin_record return a non-writing writer in dry-run mode that drains and validates framing but never creates a parent or file; retain the local pre-mkdir short-circuit and add guards asserting the destination remains absent.

findings.title: Staging space is bounded by concurrent records, not one file
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:563 — D-H claims transient space is bounded by one largest file, but crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/pipeline.rs:1206 and crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/data_plane.rs:294 show one receive task per concurrent TCP connection.
findings.predicted_failure: Several large records can simultaneously preserve their old targets and allocate staging files whose aggregate size exhausts the destination; the resulting volume-level failure remains session-fatal and may leave crash orphans.
findings.better_approach: Document the true aggregate bound and add a shared byte-weighted staging admission budget across receiver and local workers, allowing one oversize record when necessary; fault-inject low-space and concurrent-record cases.

findings.title: OpenedSourceFile cannot drive the promised handle-based fast paths
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:365 — the proposed type exposes only Box<dyn AsyncRead> and metadata, yet :456 requires passing its descriptor through the copy cascade; crates/blit-core/src/copy/file_copy/mod.rs:29 and :162-180 currently reopen paths and use concrete File handles for clone, copy_file_range, sendfile, and sparse copying.
findings.predicted_failure: Implementation must either reopen the source path and can copy a replacement inode after validation, violating A12, or fall back to buffered copying and risk failing the A17 performance requirement.
findings.better_approach: Specify a production handle variant that owns the concrete file descriptor or handle and offers same-handle metadata and copy operations, alongside a virtual fault-injection variant; refactor platform fast paths to consume it and test an atomic source-path replacement.

findings.title: The staging basename rejects valid maximum-length filenames
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:558 — staging is named .<name>.blit-<nonce>, lengthening the target's final component.
findings.predicted_failure: A target whose filename already reaches the filesystem component limit transfers today but will fail every staged attempt with a name-too-long error.
findings.better_approach: Use a fixed-length random basename such as .blit-stage-<nonce> in the validated target directory, create it atomically with create_new and collision retries, and retain the target mapping only in RecordWriter state.

findings.title: Canonical state omits two owner rulings
findings.evidence: docs/STATE.md:43 — the canonical state says D1–D4 are open, repeated at :69 and :173, while docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:4 declares D1–D6 and defines D5 and D6 at :728 and :741.
findings.predicted_failure: An owner arriving through the canonical state entry point can answer only four questions and mistakenly treat the plan as fully ruled while staging and manifest identity remain unresolved.
findings.better_approach: Change all three state references to D1–D6 and briefly identify D5 as staged streamed writes and D6 as manifest-entry identity.
